MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The original J-B Weld epoxy felt useful alongside my recent fastening and mounting purchases because it could help with small repairs where screws are not suitable.",
    "The single mini roll of duct tape felt like a practical addition for temporary fixes, with a quantity I could reasonably use for occasional maintenance."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Copper sealing washers, WaterWeld and hose clamps address specific sealing or leak repairs that I do not currently need to make.",
    "The flat washers require a particular size match; buying wood screws and drywall anchors does not establish that I need 3/8-inch washers.",
    "Metal layout fluid does not fit my current fastening and household maintenance tasks, and replacing vacuum bags does not create a need for three spray bottles.",
    "Eighteen rolls of tape and twenty-four bottles of glue exceed what I need for occasional repairs, even though the products themselves could be useful."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My fastening purchases seem to have been taken as interest in almost any workshop or repair supply, regardless of the task it serves.",
    "My purchases of large packs of nails and screws seem to have been extended to bulk adhesives and tape, although I would use those supplies at a different pace."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Specific dimensions and intended uses matter to me: a related fastener or repair part is useful only if it fits the job.",
    "Quantity matters separately from usefulness; I can use a small roll of tape without needing eighteen full-size rolls.",
    "My recent purchases cover separate needs, so vacuum bags or medicine cups should not imply that I am starting a broader cleaning or liquid-handling project."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my practical repair needs but stretched them into specialized tasks and quantities I do not currently need."
}
